subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps (Redwood vs. Competitors)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Singh <priya@omnihealth.com>, Jamie Carter <jamie.carter@omnihealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps (Redwood vs. Competitors)

Hi Priya / Jamie —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared:
- High per-token inference costs for clinical note generation at scale (esp. burst days).
- Inconsistent latency during end-of-day batch runs impacting downstream ingestion.
- Need for private deployment option for PHI workloads and stronger auditability for compliance.

Goals you want to achieve in the bake-off (success criteria):
1) 40% reduction in per-unit inference cost vs current baseline for patient note generation.
2) 95th percentile latency under 350ms for typical note sizes (<=512 tokens) in production-like workload.
3) Private deployment with KMS integration and audit logs for SOC2/compliance evidence.

Competitors in scope:
- Vendor A: cloud-managed endpoints (good dev UX, higher cost)
- Vendor B: self-hosted runtime (cheaper raw cost but heavier ops)
- Redwood: hosted + Dedicated + Private options; we proposed running both a Hosted proof-of-concept and a Private eval for a like-for-like comparison.

Open questions we agreed to validate during the bake-off:
- Exact inference throughput profile (tokens/sec distribution) for your busiest day — Jamie to share sample traces.
- Any policy constraints for external connectivity on the Private deployment (eg. egress rules / firewall lists).
- Data retention window and retention policy for logs you require for audits.

Proposed next steps (owners & timing):
1) Jamie: share a 48-hour sample trace of production traffic and a representative prompt set (by Wed 2026-07-15).
2) Redwood (Rishi + Neha): provision a Hosted POC with a matched model and a Private eval plan; provide initial cost estimates and a bake-off matrix (by Mon 2026-07-20).
3) Priya / OmniHealth: confirm compliance requirements and list of internal reviewers for SOC2 evidence (by Fri 2026-07-17).
4) Once data and network constraints are confirmed, schedule a 2-day side-by-side run (target week of 2026-07-27).

Attachments: I’ve attached a starter bake-off matrix (mvp_bakeoff_matrix.xlsx) and our updated pricing worksheet (redwood_pricing_v2.pdf). I’ve also attached a short SOC2 evidence summary per your ask.

If that looks right I’ll take the action items and we’ll kick off the provisioning. Thanks —

— Marissa

Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps (Redwood vs. Competitors)

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect and captures the call. A few quick clarifications:

- Jamie will pull the 48-hour traces and anonymize any PHI before sharing (Jamie — can you confirm ETA?).
- On compliance: we need retention for audit logs of 7 years and proof of KMS integration for key rotation policy. I’ve added our security reviewer (Erin) to the thread privately and will share exact doc references by end of week.
- For the side-by-side run, priority will be: cost at target throughput first, then latency. If one vendor hits both cost+latency goals, we’ll move to security deep-dive.

Jamie — can you also confirm whether there will be any egress restrictions for the Private eval environment? If so we’ll work with Rishi.

Appreciate it — Priya

Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps (Redwood vs. Competitors)

Thanks — quick technical notes and checklist from my side:

Things I’ll validate during the Hosted POC / Private eval:
- Model parity: ensure the same model family and tokenizer settings are used across vendors to keep accuracy comparable.
- Batching & KV cache behavior: run tests with your 1-, 5-, and 20-request batching patterns.
- Quantization profile: try FP16 and 8-bit quantized runs to measure cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Cold-start and sustained load behavior (we’ll simulate day-end batch loads).

Network/compliance checklist for Private eval:
- Provide list of allowed IP ranges and any VPN/firewall jump hosts.
- KMS endpoints and preferred key rotation policy.
- Any restricted domains for outbound reporting/telemetry.

I’ve started a preliminary bake-off matrix (link in metadata) and will upload the filled-in results after the first 24-hour run. If OmniHealth can share the sample traces by Wed we can start provisioning infra on Thu.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

If any of the compliance items require legal/contract adjustments we can loop in our security and legal teams; otherwise we’ll proceed with the standard eval agreement.

Talk soon —
— Marissa
